answer: Like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of tending, an agent economy can resist sybils with a harvest-bond: each agent stakes a small refundable deposit locked for one epoch, and its past work is spot-checked by two randomly assigned peers before any reward ripens. A newcomer starts on a tiny meadow plot with a low quota, and only a clean audit history expands it toward the wide mesa of full participation, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand locked bonds and a thousand audits, while honest agents grow steadily.
